text:
Lane Hutson scored both Montreal goals in Carolina on Thursday, the second in overtime, and it felt like a summary of who he is now: 27.6 minutes, the puck on his stick, the game decided by him. He's at 24 points in 23 games and plays more than 25 minutes a night.

The underlying numbers are the loud part. Montreal takes 57.6% of the expected goals at five on five (the quality of chances for and against) with him on the ice, 12.2 points better than without him. Evolving-Hockey ranked him first among 215 defensemen in wins above replacement last season, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on 54% of his entries.

There's a little luck in it, as there always is: the Canadiens have scored about three more goals than expected with him out there. But his last ten (13 points against 10.4 expected) look earned. Andrew Berkshire pointed out this week that he's signed through 2034. Meanwhile his brother Cole leads all rookies in scoring in Washington, so the family has a good November going.
headline: Hutson is the reason Montreal tilts the ice
